name: G.f. A(x) satisfies: A(x - A(x)^2) = x/(1-x).
comment: Conjecture: for n > 1, a(n) is odd when n = 3*2^k through 4*2^k - 1 for k >= 0. - _Paul D. Hanna_, Oct 05 2025
link: Paul D. Hanna, Table of n, a(n) for n = 1..400
formula: G.f. A(x) = Sum_{n>=1} a(n)*x^n and the related series G(x) (the g.f. of A389476) satisfy the following formulas.
(2) A(x) = G(x)/(1 - G(x)) where G(x - A(x)^2) = x.
(3) G(x) = x + A(G(x))^2 where G(x) = Series_Reversion(x - A(x)^2).
example: Let G(x) be the g.f. of A389476, which begins
then A(x) = G(x)/(1 - G(x)) and G(x - A(x)^2) = x.
program: (PARI) {a(n) = my(A=x+2*x^2, B=x/(1+x+x*O(x^n))); for(i=1,n, A=serreverse(B - subst(A,x,B)^2)); polcoef(A,n)}
